newsitem.title: CANADA: Alberta wheat yield forecast seen above average.
newsitem.headline: Alberta wheat yield forecast seen above average.

text.p: Alberta's wheat yields on Thursday were forecast to exceed the five-year average as soil moisture levelled off to lower levels in the wet northern districts and rose to more adquate levels in the south, crop specialists said.

"We've got good growth," said Wendy Boje, Alberta Agriculture crop statistician. "Statistics Canada last week, according to their satelite imagery, showed Alberta crops were doing better than Saskatchewan or Manitoba."
Spring wheat was expected to yield 39.5 bushels an acre compared to the five-year average of 36.9 bu/ac, she said.
Spring wheat is Alberta's biggest crop at 6.565 million acres according to Statistics Canada's June 27 estimate.
Alberta saw excess soil moisture in the northern half and less than adequate moisture in the south through to mid June.

The damp northwest and northeast of Alberta had drier conditions in the week ended June 30 which lowered soil moisture to 60 to 90 percent of optimum capacity, down from more than 90 percent which was excessive, said Rick Raddatz, Environment Canada's soil scientist.
Southern Alberta's arid area retracted to Calgary to Lethbridge from Calgary, Lethbridge, Medicine Hat and Empress.
That area has less than 30 percent of its maximum soil moisture capacity.
Southern Alberta accounts for most of the province's durum wheat and winter wheat output.
Alberta Ag set durum yields at 40 bu/ac versus the five year average of 35.2 bu/ac while winter wheat was forecast at 40 bu/ac compared to the five year average of 38 bu/ac.
Oats, however, were expected to yield 66 bu/ac compared to the five year average of 67.2 bu/ac, Alberta Ag's Boje said.
"I've pegged it below the five year average because of where it's being grown in the northeast and northwest and it's very wet there so that may be optimistic," Boje said.
Barley yield was pegged by Alberta Ag at 60 bu/ac compared to the five year average of 59 bu/ac.
Canola output was forecast by Alberta Ag to reach 23.5 bu/ac below the five year average of 23.7 bu/ac.
